text: Synthetic homotopy theory differs from classical homotopy theory in that:
choices: it uses topological spaces as primitives
it works entirely within HoTT — spaces are types, paths are identity proofs, without needing explicit point-set topology
explanation: Synthetic: work in HoTT directly. Types are ∞-groupoids, identity types are paths, HITs are building blocks of spaces. Classical homotopy theory is 'analytic' (uses point-set topology as a foundation).
